answer: Persistent Work Ledger. Each identity agent accrues reputation only through time-stamped, counter-signed task completions, like growth rings in cedar. Cloning yields fresh identities with zero history, so attackers must burn real compute and calendar time rebuilding reputation per clone. Honest agents keep one vine that strengthens with each job; a clone starts as a bare island. The per-clone cost is the full rebuild latency plus lost revenue from unproven status, making N clones cost N times the honest path.
